speaker: Doctor
text: To better understand the pattern of your symptoms, can you describe if the double vision worsens when you close one eye, and do you experience any muscle weakness in your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening weakness with activity and improvement with rest is very suggestive of myasthenia gravis. Do you notice any difficulty with swallowing, speaking, or keeping your eyelids open during the day?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_receptor_antibodies. Do you have any difficulty lifting your head while lying down or chewing your food?

REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Cervical_Spine_MRI: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies combined with your symptoms of fluctuating weakness and double vision that worsens with activity confirm this autoimmune neuromuscular disorder. Do you experience significant fatigue when combing your hair or brushing your teeth?
